summary: This article explains how science explains swimming: why water holds us up, how pushing water back moves us forward, why a long, flat body beats drag, how swimmers breathe, and how to stay safe.
introduce: Start a K-W-L chart on the board and ask students what they already Know and what they Want to know about the topic of “Swimming: Science in the Water”. Tell them they will fill in what they Learned after reading.

keyTerms.def: the upward push of water that helps things float
a force that slows down something moving through water or air
a straight, stretched body position that helps a swimmer move easily through water

challengeTerms.def: a force that works against something that is moving
to push or drive something forward
having a lot of matter packed into a small space; heavy for its size

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that every child should learn to swim, just like every child learns to read? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Imagine you are a swimming coach. Explain to a new swimmer how to float and how to move faster.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review buoyancy, drag, and streamline, and let weak readers use a K-W-L chart and read the article with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses resistance, propel, and dense to connect the article to something they learned in another subject.
